title: Phantasm
description:
## **Phantasm** — live actors for Skyrim menus

A renderer that draws Skyrim's characters and items on their own: posed, lit and framed, for pages and pictures instead of the game's own view.

**Coming to SkyrimNet**
- In SkyrimNet's next release, OmniSight takes its pictures of characters and items through Phantasm, so the descriptions SkyrimNet writes come from a clean, well-lit shot of the person or the gear, not whatever happens to be on screen.

**In SeverActions**
- Draws the Outfits mirror, the 3D item views and the automatic faces you see across its pages.

**For mod authors**
- Other mods can use it through a small C API.

## Works on Skyrim SE, AE and VR.
author: severause
changelog:
## Phantasm 1.2.0


**Fixes**
- First-person body mods (Improved Camera): first-person views of the player no longer show a pointed neck, missing arms or missing back weapons
- Bodies with more than 128 bones (UBE soft-body with Bone Limit Extender) now pose with the character; up to 256 bones per piece
- Doubled-triangle hair (many Sims 4 conversions) no longer shows dark and light flakes

**Settings in the game**
- SKSE Menu Framework's Mod Control Panel (Phantasm > Settings), or with Magelight UI the page Scroll Lock opens. Changes hold at once and are written back to `Phantasm.ini`, comments kept. Both optional

**Experimental: neural rendering (off by default)**
- NVIDIA DLSS NR on the character pictures mods ask Phantasm for, and optionally on live views. Turn it on from the settings page (**Scroll Lock** with Magelight UI, or the Mod Control Panel), or with `[NeuralRendering] Enabled = 1` in `Phantasm.ini`
- Uses the `nvngx_dlssnr.dll` your neural rendering mod installed and follows that mod's settings 
- Runs inside the game from Phantasm's own `PhantasmNRInProc.dll` (no NVIDIA code, nothing to install beyond your driver); costs several hundred MB of memory while on

**For mod authors** (gate on `pluginVersion >= 10100`)
- `aim=face`: the camera stays on the actor's face, taken from where their head looks, so a paired-animation partner turned around is still seen face on. Also for Portrait stills via `RequestStillHinted`
- `zoom` (0.5 to 3) for Portrait stills: the face alone for a badge or round avatar, crown kept
- `scale` (0.5 to 2) for actor views and `scene` entries: draw actors at a multiple of their size while a clip plays, so paired animations line up
